prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Redraw the treasure chest in image 1 to belong unmistakably to the SAME GAME ART FAMILY as images 2 and 3. The user rejects image 1's current art style. A small colour correction is not enough: repaint its materials and simplify its shapes.
REFERENCE ROLES: image 1 is the REJECTED chest edit target, retain only the functional identity of a single closed treasure chest. Image 2 is the APPROVED GRIMOIRE SPRITE, the authoritative reference for painting technique, softened chunky bevels, restrained detail, navy outlines and muted palette. Image 3 is the CURRENT DUNGEON, authoritative for 2:1 ground-plane camera, subdued contrast and scale.
Make ONE compact, squat closed treasure chest, with a low gently arched lid and thick soft-chamfered edges. About 1.4 width to 1 depth. Main panels are muted dark burgundy-brown stained wood, visibly wooden but with only three or four broad painted plank shapes, like the simple plum leather masses of the book reference. Thick dark blue-gray iron bands and substantial shaped corner guards use exactly the slate iron appearance of the book's metal fittings and the dungeon stones. They should have two or three broad shading tones and cool painted edge accents. A single chunky central aged-brass/gold lock plate with a large dark keyhole makes the TREASURE function immediately recognizable. Use gold sparingly on that lock and a few catches, NOT huge polished gold hoops. Make it crafted and slightly sinister, with a few broad clipped/notched corners, no skull or monster face, no delicate ornament, no tiny metal rivets. No magical aura, gems, emissive runes or external effects for this basic chest.
The finish must be stylized hand-painted cartoon game art, calm and graphic at 90-100 pixels wide: clear colour masses, soft bevels, dark contours. NOT realistic wood, NOT glossy golden metal, NOT a shiny 3D product render, NOT noisy painterly microtexture. Readable in miniature, more in common with the approved grimoire than with a realistic treasure illustration.
CAMERA: orthographic 2:1 dimetric game view, verticals upright. Both straight base-edge families must have slopes +0.5 and -0.5 in image space; the first chest's short-side edge was too steep. No perspective convergence, no front-facing inventory icon. Show top, broad front and short side; flat grounded base, no long feet or pedestal. Light from upper-left, simple navy shade on right.
OUTPUT: the single complete repainted chest only, centered with clear transparent margins, native alpha. Preserve transparency. No book, dungeon, paving, ground patch, cast/drop shadow, extra objects, text, checkerboard or background.
